title: Small generating maps for an accessible reflective localization
statement: Use the universe, presentability and accessibility conventions of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and the coherent mapping-space conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Let $\mathcal V$ be presentable and let $L:\mathcal V\rightleftarrows\mathcal U:i$ be a reflective adjunction with $i$ fully faithful and the endofunctor $iL$ accessible. There is a small set $S$ of arrows of $\mathcal V$ such that the essential image of $i$ consists exactly of the $S$-local objects. Here $Z$ is $S$-local if $\operatorname{Map}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in S$.

source.place: HTT Proposition 5.5.4.2(3) and the strongly reflective subcategory characterization following Proposition 5.5.4.16 (printed p. 483). No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result; online reference, not archived.

proof.text:
Put $T=iL$. The category $\mathcal V$ has small mapping spaces by presentability, and full faithfulness identifies each $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal U}(u,v)$ with the small space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(iu,iv)$ up to equivalence. Thus $\mathcal U$ is locally small as required by the adjunction statement below. The given adjunction has a coherent unit $\eta:\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal V}\to T$ and the natural mapping-space bifunctor equivalence, with its unit interpretation, of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion]. For every $X\in\mathcal V$ and $u\in\mathcal U$, full faithfulness of $i$ and adjunction give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(TX,iu)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal U}(LX,u)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(X,iu).$$
Their composite is precomposition with $\eta_X$: a map $a:LX\to u$ goes to $i(a)\eta_X$ by the unit description of the adjunction. Thus every object in the essential image of $i$ is local for every unit map. If $Z\simeq iu$, postcomposition with that equivalence gives the same assertion for $Z$.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.2(1), first direction; section 5.2.7, mapping-space localization adjunction

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-compact-approximation] to the single accessible infinity category $\mathcal V$ and its accessible endofunctor $T$. The category is accessible because it is presentable. Accessible for $T$ means that it preserves small $\rho$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular $\rho$, as specified in the cited statement. Obtain an infinite regular $\tau$ for which $\mathcal V$ is $\tau$-accessible, $T$ preserves small $\tau$-filtered colimits, and $\mathcal V^\tau$ is essentially small. Choose a small quasicategory $D$ with an equivalence $D\to\mathcal V^\tau$ and denote its vertex images by $d$. Set
$$S=\{\eta_d:d\longrightarrow Td\mid d\text{ is the image of a vertex of }D\}.$$
This is a small set: it is indexed by the small set $D_0$. Only this set of specified unit maps is used; neither all arrows of $\mathcal V$ nor an entire large compact-source slice is used as an indexing set.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.2(3), proof of (ii) implies (iii), printed p. 476; Proposition 5.4.2.9 for a common accessibility rank

proof.text: Let $X\in\mathcal V$. By $\tau$-accessibility as defined in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], choose a small $\tau$-filtered diagram $p:I\to\mathcal V$ of $\tau$-compact objects and a colimiting cocone $p\to X$. Since $T$ preserves these colimits, $Tp\to TX$ is colimiting. The coherent unit restricted to the cocone gives a cocone of arrows $\eta_{p(q)}:p(q)\to Tp(q)$ with apex $\eta_X:X\to TX$. By the pointwise-colimit statement of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], this is a colimiting cocone in $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal V)$. Hence every unit is a small filtered colimit of unit maps on compact objects. All colimits here have small indexing quasicategory $I$; $\mathcal V$ supplies them by presentability.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.2(3), (ii) implies (iii), printed p. 476; expanded compact-presentation argument in place of the invocation of Proposition 5.3.5.10

proof.text:
Suppose $Z$ is $S$-local. For each $q\in I$, choose an equivalence $e:d\simeq p(q)$ from one of the representatives in Step 2. Naturality gives $T(e)\eta_d\simeq\eta_{p(q)}e$. Choose an inverse to $e$ and its two inverse $2$-simplices. Applying the simplicial functor $T$ gives an inverse to $T(e)$ with both inverse witnesses. Precomposition with $e$ and $T(e)$ therefore gives equivalences of mapping spaces: precomposition with their chosen inverses supplies inverse maps, and the inverse $2$-simplices supply the inverse homotopies. The naturality square identifies the test for $\eta_{p(q)}$ with the test for $\eta_d\in S$ under these equivalences. Consequently every map $\operatorname{Map}(Tp(q),Z)\to\operatorname{Map}(p(q),Z)$ is an equivalence. The coherent unit gives these maps as a transformation of diagrams on $I^{\mathrm{op}}$. It is an equivalence by the componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]; its limit is an equivalence as well, by applying the limit universal property to this transformation and its inverse. The natural contravariant mapping-space colimit formula of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identifies that limit map with
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(TX,Z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(X,Z),\qquad h\longmapsto h\eta_X.$$
More explicitly the two sides identify with $\lim_{q\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(Tp(q),Z)$ and $\lim_{q\in I^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(p(q),Z)$, respectively, and naturality of the colimit formulas identifies the displayed map with precomposition by the apex of the arrow cocone in Step 3. Thus $S$-locality implies locality for every unit map, including $\eta_Z$.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.2(3), (ii) implies (iii), printed p. 476; natural representable-colimit calculation

proof.text: Take $X=Z$ in Step 4. Surjectivity on components gives $r:TZ\to Z$ with $r\eta_Z\simeq\operatorname{id}_Z$. Since $TZ=i(LZ)$ lies in the image of $i$, Step 1 says that precomposition with $\eta_Z$ gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(TZ,TZ)\to\operatorname{Map}(Z,TZ)$. The two maps $\eta_Zr$ and $\operatorname{id}_{TZ}$ have homotopic composites with $\eta_Z$, because $\eta_Zr\eta_Z\simeq\eta_Z$. Injectivity on components of this equivalence gives $\eta_Zr\simeq\operatorname{id}_{TZ}$. Thus $r$ is a two-sided homotopy inverse to $\eta_Z$ and $Z\simeq TZ=i(LZ)$, so $Z$ is in the essential image. Conversely Step 1 applied to the maps of the specified set $S$ shows that every object of that essential image is $S$-local. This proves the required equality of object classes without invoking a separate retract-closure theorem.

source.place: Proposition 5.5.4.2(1), converse, printed p. 474; explicit two-sided inverse argument

lean.note: Defines the explicit arrow model, canonical mapping-space composition and precomposition test, essential-image predicate, and accessible endofunctor predicate used by the theorem. The theorem states exactly that an accessible reflective localization with fully faithful right adjoint is generated by a small set of arrows, with local objects characterized by weak equivalences on mapping spaces. All data definitions are real constructions; only the theorem proof is postponed.
